title: Hidden matching in one-way communication

problem.name: Hidden matching in one-way communication
problem.statement_latex: Alice holds $x\in\{0,1\}^n$ and Bob a perfect matching $M$ on $[n]$. After one message from Alice, Bob outputs an edge $(i,j)\in M$ and the bit $x_i\oplus x_j$, with success at least $2/3$. Complexity counts one-way communicated bits or qubits.
problem.statement_text: Alice holds $x\in\{0,1\}^n$ and Bob a perfect matching $M$ on $[n]$. After one message from Alice, Bob outputs an edge $(i,j)\in M$ and the bit $x_i\oplus x_j$, with success at least $2/3$. Complexity counts one-way communicated bits or qubits.

strength.description_latex: $\Theta(\sqrt n/\log n)$ communication reduction against the public-coin classical optimum.
strength.description_text: $\Theta(\sqrt n/\log n)$ communication reduction against the public-coin classical optimum.

evidence.description_latex: The classical lower bound holds even with shared randomness.
evidence.description_text: The classical lower bound holds even with shared randomness.

hardware.description_latex: $\log_2n$ transmitted qubits ideally; coherent-state optical variants have experimental demonstrations.
hardware.description_text: $\log_2n$ transmitted qubits ideally; coherent-state optical variants have experimental demonstrations.

quantum.headline_latex: $\lceil\log_2n\rceil$ qubits with exact success. Alice sends $n^{-1/2}\sum_i(-1)^{x_i}|i\rangle$; Bob measures in the basis $(|i\rangle\pm|j\rangle)/\sqrt2$ for edges in $M$.
quantum.headline_text: $\lceil\log_2n\rceil$ qubits with exact success. Alice sends $n^{-1/2}\sum_i(-1)^{x_i}|i\rangle$; Bob measures in the basis $(|i\rangle\pm|j\rangle)/\sqrt2$ for edges in $M$.

classical.headline_latex: $\Omega(\sqrt n)$ randomized classical bits are necessary. Shared randomness enables a matching $O(\sqrt n)$ birthday-paradox protocol; sending sampled indices explicitly costs $O(\sqrt n\log n)$ with private randomness.
